exposure.note: Measured from the compose files, not asserted. pod_internal is expose-only; a published port is what makes a surface pod_external.
exposure.evidence: Measured 2026-09-05 from the deployment files, per rule 4. runtimes/mind-pod/docker-compose.yml has ONE ports: entry -- line 98, service config, "13003:3000". runtimes/mind-pod/app/extract/compose.yml has three -- line 30 back "13002:3000", line 71 front "13000:3000", line 99 config "13003:3000". Every other service is expose-only. oxigraph binds 0.0.0.0:7878 (docker-compose.yml:156) INSIDE the pod network and has no ports: entry, so it is not host-published. A published port is what makes a surface pod_external rather than pod_internal, so the services absent from those lists are the pod-internal ones. DISCREPANCY, recorded rather than smoothed over: none of those ports names a host interface, so Docker binds 0.0.0.0 and they are reachable from anywhere the host is, not only from the host. spec/scopes.md defines pod_external as "reachable from the host, never from the open internet". Making that true means binding 127.0.0.1 in the compose files; until then the measurement and the doctrine disagree, and the measurement is what is here.

invariants: callers allowlisted per seam (*_CALLERS), Bearer tokens
401/403 plus envelope to an unauthenticated or unallowlisted caller is designed behaviour, not an error path
